questions.question: A valid checkout fails whenever the optional recommendations service times out. Which invariant best expresses graceful degradation?
options: Recommendations must always be fresh
A recommendation outage cannot stop a valid order
Every request must make the same number of network calls
Checkout must own the recommendation database
questions.explanation: Recommendations are optional enrichment. The checkout path should complete without them while the outage is visible to operators.

questions.question: A service receives 4,000 requests per second and one worker sustains 800 requests per second at the target latency. What is the minimum worker count before headroom?
questions.explanation: Divide demand by per-worker capacity: 4,000 / 800 = 5. Production capacity needs additional headroom for failures and uneven load.

questions.question: Which change is the clearest sign of loose coupling between two services?
options: Both services write the same private database tables
A consumer depends on a versioned public contract instead of the producer's internal storage
The services are deployed on the same host
The consumer retries indefinitely on every failure
questions.explanation: An explicit, versioned contract lets the consumer depend on supported behavior rather than the producer's implementation details.

questions.question: When should a system fail fast rather than continue in a reduced mode?
options: When an optional image service is temporarily unavailable
When a request violates an authorization or data invariant before an irreversible write
When a cached profile is older than a few seconds but still within policy
When a non-critical analytics event is delayed
questions.explanation: Invalid authorization or data must be rejected before it can propagate or create an irreversible side effect.

questions.question: Why is an interface with one implementation not automatically an application of the open/closed principle?
options: Interfaces make code slower
It may add indirection without a real independent variation to extend
Open/closed applies only to databases
Every interface must have exactly three implementations
questions.explanation: Open/closed is valuable when stable orchestration needs to support a real variation. Abstraction without that pressure can obscure a simple design.

questions.question: A payment worker only needs to publish to one queue, but its token can read customer data and administer all queues. Which principle is violated most directly?
options: Horizontal scaling
Least privilege
Caching
Single responsibility
questions.explanation: Least privilege grants only the permissions needed for the task, limiting the blast radius of a compromised worker or credential.
